transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... it's dispatch and compliance. They’ve been tracking my route changes through the computer system. I know they are. And there are these little comments on the radio... which, actually, the radio in my rig has been acting up so much lately. It gets this weird high-pitched static right when I drive past the old water tower on Route 9. I told the mechanic about it, but he just started talking about the alternator. My dad used to fix alternators in his garage, he had this huge collection of vintage wrenches. He was always losing the 10-millimeter one, though. Everyone loses the 10-millimeter, I guess. 

But anyway, even when people say it’s just normal oversight for the company, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. They're definitely reporting on me. I don't know why they'd care so much, especially since half of them don't even bother to wash their own windshields before a shift. It's just a basic safety thing, you know? A dirty windshield catches the glare.
About how long has this been going on with dispatch and the other drivers?

Well, the computer tracking and those comments on the radio... it's been really clear to me for about two months now. Yeah, two months. That was right around when the leaves started dropping, which is honestly my favorite time to drive. The foliage up north is just beautiful. Although, you have to be so careful about wet leaves on the off-ramps. They get slicker than black ice. I remember this one time I was driving my old Subaru—not my rig, just my personal car—and I slid right past a stop sign. Luckily no one was coming. It was a Tuesday, I think, because I was on my way to get tacos. There's this little food truck that parks by the hardware store on Tuesdays, and they make their own salsa verde from scratch. The guy who runs it is always wearing this bright orange beanie, even in the middle of summer. I don't know how he doesn't overheat standing next to the grill like that.
Have you noticed a decreased need for sleep lately, where you sleep much less but still feel energized?

Sleep? No, I don't think so. I sleep about the same as I always do. Usually, I'm pretty tired after a long shift, you know? Especially if I've been driving through the mountains. The elevation changes really take it out of you. Plus, the heater in my cab is so loud when you crank it up. It has this rattle that sounds exactly like a spray paint can when you shake it. I used to paint murals when I was in high school—nothing illegal, just on the side of my uncle's barn. He had this old dairy farm, but he didn't actually have any cows anymore. Just a bunch of barn cats that would sleep on the tractor tires. There was this one orange tabby that would always try to climb into my paint bucket. Orange cats are always the craziest ones, aren't they? I read somewhere that coat color is linked to personality in cats, but I don't know if that's actually true or just something people say on the internet. But yeah, no, my sleep is fine.

Voices? No... I mean, I don't hear people talking to me in my head or anything like that, if that's what you mean. It's just the radio stuff I mentioned. And, well, the normal sounds of the rig. When you haul an empty trailer, the wind catches it like a giant sail, and it makes this awful howling noise through the weather stripping on the passenger door. I tried to patch it with duct tape a few weeks ago. 

Duct tape really does fix almost anything, doesn't it? My grandfather used to swear by it. He kept this massive, heavy-duty roll of silver tape in his tackle box. We used to go fishing down at Lake Oconee when I was a kid. The bass there get huge. I actually caught a five-pounder when I was ten, and we fried it up that same night with a big batch of hushpuppies. I haven't had a really good hushpuppy in years, though. Most of the diners at the truck stops just make them way too dry now, almost like you're eating a mouthful of cornmeal sand. You really need to put diced jalapeños or onions in the batter to keep the moisture right, otherwise they just fall apart when you dip them.

Outside of work? Um... well, I guess I haven't really been doing much. I used to sing with this community choir, and I'd always have the softball team over for drinks after our games, but I just... I don't feel like doing any of that anymore. I don't know why. Most days after my shift, I just come home and sit at the kitchen table. I'll have my planner open, thinking I should make dinner or call someone, but I just sit there. I can't make myself start anything. 

It's a nice planner, too. I bought it at this little stationery shop downtown that smells like lavender and old paper. They sell these fountain pens there that are just gorgeous, with the little gold nibs. I tried to learn calligraphy once, a few years ago. I bought all the ink and the special thick paper, but I always ended up smudging it because I'm left-handed. Being left-handed is such a pain when you're writing, you know? Your hand just drags right through the wet ink. My third-grade teacher actually tried to make me write with my right hand, but my mom came down to the school and threw an absolute fit. She was wearing this bright yellow raincoat that day, which she always wore even when it was barely drizzling. She said it made her feel like a sunflower. Sunflowers are supposed to track the sun across the sky, but I read that they only do that when they're young. Once they mature, they just face east. I wonder why east, specifically. Maybe because of the sunrise?
